REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for sorghum (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-QLD-2020-0199 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 15 May 2020 and the current registration period extends to 14 May 2023. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Scott Mitchell is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2009. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered area is the entire farm property at 102 Gore Highway, Dalby QLD 4405, totalling approximately 90.0 hectares. All paddocks, laneways, buildings and infrastructure are included in the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: sorghum is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of sorghum. Total storage capacity is approximately 8,000 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No site-specific hygiene and sanitation program documented for Dandenong Fresh Pack Pty Ltd. General industry practices are referenced but no cleaning schedules, chemicals, personnel hygiene procedures or records are defined.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Dandenong Fresh Pack Pty Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

Pest Control Program (EF-PCP-001) — Integrated Pest Management:
• Rodent control: 18 perimeter bait stations (Bromadiolone, tamper-resistant boxes), mapped in Bait Station Plan.
• Insect control: phosphine fumigation of stored grain when insect activity detected by pitfall traps.
• Bird exclusion: all silo vents and openings bird-proofed; netting installed at conveyor gallery ends.
• Monitoring: monthly visual inspection of all bait stations (Form GCE-PC-01); bi-monthly pitfall trap check; grain temperature probe weekly.
• Licensed pest contractor: Annual review by APC-licensed contractor; report filed.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Dandenong Fresh Pack Pty Ltd. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.

Failed Goods Management Procedure (GCE-FGP-001):
• If a lot fails mycotoxin, pesticide or ergot tests: segregate immediately; label silo as 'HOLD'; notify Quality Manager.
• Blending of failed lots with passing lots to achieve compliance is NOT permitted for mycotoxin or ergot failures.
• Re-testing: one re-test from additional sample permitted if initial result near threshold; documented.
• Downgrade: failed export lots may be sold as domestic feed grain after grower consultation.
• Rejected at port: consignment returned to registered establishment; re-inspect; document non-conformance; notify DAFF.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (GCE-PSP-001):
• After fumigation, grain remains in sealed silo until DAFF sampling. No grain movement between sampling and loading.
• Transport unit inspected for cleanliness and freedom from infestation before loading (Form GCE-TU-01).
• Sealed containers: seal number recorded on dispatch docket; communicated to receiving port.
• Co-mingling of export-cleared grain with non-cleared grain is prohibited at all times.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Western Downs Grain is a registered export establishment located at 102 Gore Highway, Dalby QLD 4405, QLD. The establishment holds RE Number RE-QLD-2020-0199 and is registered to handle and export Mangoes under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Mangoes.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

T5 LED fluorescent panels on 600 mm spacing — 550 lux at floor level throughout processing area. Task lighting above grading line at 600 lux. Loading dock: 400 W LED floods at 418 lux. Emergency lighting on dedicated UPS circuit.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Self-contained amenities unit: 2 flush toilets, urinal, 3 hand basins — hot/cold water, liquid soap dispensers, paper towels, hand sanitiser. Sited at main processing entry (<15 m from packing line). Additional wash station at grading line head-of-line position.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Wall cladding is corrugated zincalume (762 profile) fixed directly to the steel frame with horizontal ribs at 76 mm intervals. These horizontal ledges accumulate grain dust, pest material and moisture. Product residue lodges in the corrugation valleys and cannot be removed with standard pressure washing. Floor is unsealed reinforced concrete from 2010 — surface carbonation has created a friable, dusty surface layer that sheds during sweeping.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Pest exclusion features: (1) all gaps >6 mm in the building envelope sealed; (2) ventilation openings screened with 6 mm galvanised mesh; (3) all doors have rubber or brush seals at threshold and jambs; (4) drainage openings covered with SS mesh inserts; (5) no internal ledges >50 mm depth without ≥45° slope; (6) equipment on feet to eliminate floor-level harbourage. Inspected by licensed technician every 6 months.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Waste infrastructure: (1) floor drains to grease interceptor → licensed trade waste; (2) solid product waste in sealed 240 L bins at processing line discharge — removed to covered bunded external skip, collected by contractor twice weekly; (3) packaging waste in baler at external waste bay; (4) dust and fines via bag filter — bags sealed and removed weekly. All collection points have contained, cleanable surfaces.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Control System (Doc WCS-001): defines (a) waste stream classification, (b) daily/weekly/post-production cleaning tasks, (c) responsible personnel, (d) waste contractor schedule, (e) emergency spill response. Compliance records in digital operations log. Internal audit quarterly.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Establishment condition — most recent internal inspection: processing hall floor clean, drains clear; grading equipment wiped down post-use, no residue on contact surfaces; wall linings free from dust and condensation staining; chemical store tidy with labelled containers; waste bins emptied and clean. Condition consistent with good hygiene practices.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Establishment pest-free: no rodent activity (no droppings, gnaw marks or runs observed); insect pheromone traps — current catches below threshold (3 moths/week vs 10 moths/week threshold); grain probe sampling negative for live insects; bird deterrents in place and effective; all bait stations serviceable.

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Western Downs Grain used in horticultural packing and cold-chain export operations for Tomatoes. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Tomatoes during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay

After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line

After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line

End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms

Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System
Records are kept by the establishment manager. Location: manager's office. Staff are advised to confirm cleaning completion with the manager at the end of each shift.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Independent third-party hygiene audits are conducted twice annually. Between audits, internal verification is carried out by the establishment manager using a standardised checklist.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

If a cleaning check reveals an area is not compliant with this plan, the area is isolated and re-cleaned. The supervisor completes a Corrective Action Report within 24 hours. The report is reviewed by management and used to update training or procedures where required.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The establishment was inspected by the Establishment Manager on 6 November 2025. All production areas, storage facilities, and amenities were confirmed clean and free of product residue, pest activity, and hygiene deficiencies.
